conditions.title: Observing conditions
conditions.placeholder: Set your location, then refresh the conditions.
conditions.disclaimer: Forecasts provided by Open-Meteo. The embedded map shows a satellite estimate of light pollution, not a measurement of the real sky from the ground.

conditions.unknownPosition: Unknown position. Use the location icon to authorize geolocation, then refresh.
conditions.loading: Loading weather conditions and local sky…
conditions.hourlyUnavailable: Hourly forecasts unavailable for this date and time; current weather values are displayed for reference.
conditions.noIndexData: Weather data do not allow computing an index.
conditions.indexBasis: indicative index computed from clouds, precipitation, humidity, wind and visibility; it does not measure astronomical transparency or light pollution.
conditions.howToReadText: Clouds: sky cover; temperature: comfort and dew risk; rain: precipitation risk; humidity: possible condensation; wind: comfort and instrument stability; visibility: meteorological range, which does not guarantee a transparent sky. The weather index is indicative and does not replace on-site sky assessment.
conditions.sourceFull: Weather: Open-Meteo. Map: Light Pollution Map (lightpollutionmap.app), satellite estimate of light pollution.
conditions.weatherUnavailable: Weather forecasts unavailable. Check the internet connection; the light pollution map remains accessible below.
conditions.sourceMapOnly: Map: Light Pollution Map (lightpollutionmap.app), satellite estimate of light pollution.
conditions.helpClouds: Estimated sky cover percentage: the less there is, the better faint objects can stand out.
conditions.helpTemp: Air temperature. The felt temperature may be different; plan for appropriate clothing.
conditions.helpRain: Probability or quantity of precipitation forecast. A shower can interrupt the observation and wet the equipment.
conditions.helpWind: Wind speed at 10 m. Wind can affect telescope stability and make the cold more sensitive.
conditions.helpHumidity: Relative humidity: with cooling, it can favor dew and condensation on optics.
conditions.helpVisibility: Estimated meteorological visibility, not a measure of astronomical transparency or light pollution.
conditions.hourlyForecastLocalTime: (local time), at the nearest full hour to the chosen start time

visibleNow.title: Visible now
visibleNow.timeControlsAria: Date and time for visible objects
visibleNow.searchAria: Search in the deep sky catalogue
visibleNow.searchLabel: Search for an object, even below the horizon
visibleNow.helpText: The selection favours objects above 10° and suggests a few targets according to their type and catalogue magnitude. The 'Spotting' label is an educational estimate based on height, type, magnitude and chosen equipment, not a guarantee of visibility. Light pollution, transparency, surface brightness and experience change the result; diffuse objects can be difficult even with a favourable integrated magnitude. When calculable, culmination indicates when the target passes highest in the sky.
visibleNow.disclaimer: Visibility depends on the location and date selected. Presence above the horizon does not guarantee that the object is visible to the naked eye.

starHop.diagramTitle: Diagram of the path between an anchor star and a target
starHop.diagramDesc: Interactive celestial sphere calculated from real star coordinates. Drag the sphere to rotate it; use the buttons or the wheel to zoom. Stars located behind the sphere are not displayed.
starHop.sphereCaption: Celestial sphere · free rotation, schematic orientation
starHop.sphereHelp: The sphere uses real celestial coordinates. Drag to rotate it, use the wheel or buttons to enlarge or reduce the sphere, and 'Recenter' to find the complete route. The rotation of the sphere is a manipulation of the model: it does not represent the actual movement of the sky.

starHop.noStepCalculated: No step calculable with the available coordinates.

ui.expertStar: Milky Way star. Displayed parameters depend on measurements available in the catalogue.
ui.expertPlanet: Solar System planet; its position is recalculated for the selected observation date.
ui.expertDwarfPlanet: Solar System dwarf planet; its position is estimated from simplified orbital elements.
ui.expertComet: Comet: its position and brightness are estimated from a simplified orbital model. Comet brightness predictions remain highly uncertain.
ui.expertMinorPlanet: Minor planet: its position is estimated from orbital elements and a simplified Keplerian model.
ui.expertGalaxy: Gravitational system composed of stars, gas, dust and dark matter.
ui.expertNebula: Interstellar cloud of gas and/or dust, associated with star formation or evolution.
ui.expertCluster: Group of bound or related stars, observed in the same region of the sky.
ui.discoveryStar1: is a star in the Milky Way
ui.discoveryStar2: . Its color and apparent brightness help compare it to neighboring stars; its twinkling also depends on the atmosphere.
ui.discoveryPlanet: is a planet in the Solar System. Its distance, apparent size and perceptible details change according to its position in its orbit; a very bright point to the naked eye does not necessarily reveal its surface.
ui.discoveryDwarfPlanet: is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun. Its position on the map is calculated with a simplified orbital model; a professional ephemeris remains preferable for high-precision pointing.
ui.discoveryComet: is a comet: a small icy body that can release gas and dust as it approaches the Sun. Its position is calculated by a simplified orbital model; its actual brightness may differ strongly from predictions.
ui.discoveryMinorPlanet: is an asteroid orbiting the Sun. Its position on the map is calculated with simplified orbital propagation; a professional ephemeris remains preferable for high-precision pointing.
ui.discoveryGalaxy: is a galaxy: a vast ensemble of stars, gas and dust bound by gravity. To the naked eye or binoculars, it most often appears as a faint diffuse glow, very sensitive to sky quality.
ui.discoveryNebula: is a nebula, a cloud of gas and/or dust. Depending on its nature, it can illuminate forming stars or consist of matter ejected by a dying star; its details depend heavily on the sky and the instrument.
ui.discoveryCluster: is a star cluster. An open cluster draws a group of stars in the Milky Way; a globular cluster forms a very dense ball of ancient stars. Binoculars often reveal numerous members.
ui.discoveryGeneric: is a celestial object whose appearance depends on its nature, sky quality and the instrument used.
